Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Departmental stores are usually located in —

questions.answer: C

questions.answer: D

questions.q: Which of the following is a middleman?
questions.answer: B

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Match: (i) Bulk Breaking (ii) Bulk Buying with (a) Wholesaler (b) Retailer.
questions.answer: (i) Bulk breaking – (b) Retailer (buys in bulk and sells in small quantities); (ii) bulk buying – (a) Wholesaler.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: ______ refers to buying goods from the manufacturers or wholesalers and selling them to final consumers.
questions.answer: Retail trade.

questions.q: Give two characteristics of internal trade.
questions.answer: Buying and selling take place within the home country; payment is in the home country's currency.

questions.q: Write WT for wholesale trade and RT for retail trade: (a) dealing in limited variety; (b) buying goods from wholesalers for resale; (c) grading and packaging; (d) located near residential areas.
questions.answer: (a) WT. (b) RT. (c) WT. (d) RT.

questions.q: Identify the type of retailing: (a) A store dealing in books. (b) A store with all varieties of one brand. (c) Selling goods on the pavement.
questions.answer: (a) Single line store. (b) Speciality store. (c) Itinerant retailing (hawkers).

questions.q: Name any three types of large-scale retail trade.
questions.answer: Departmental store, multiple shops and supermarket (also consumer cooperative store, mail order and franchise).

questions.q: Correct the following: (a) A wholesaler has a direct link with consumers. (b) The capital required is less in wholesale trade.
questions.answer: (a) A wholesaler has a direct link with producers. (b) The capital required is large in wholesale trade.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) The producer is a middleman. (ii) Too many middlemen increase the price.
questions.answer: (i) False. (ii) True.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain why intermediaries are used despite adding to cost.
questions.answer: They increase the efficiency of distribution by bulk breaking, storing, financing and making goods available to consumers near them.

questions.q: State any two features of internal trade.
questions.answer: Trade within the geographical boundaries of a country and payment in the home currency.

questions.q: What is itinerant retailing?
questions.answer: Small-scale retail trade in which retailers move around and sell goods directly to consumers without a fixed shop.

questions.q: What is a franchise form of retail trade? State any one feature.
questions.answer: A franchisor permits the franchisee to use its brand name and business system for a fee; the franchisee owns and runs the outlet under the franchisor's guidelines.

questions.q: Who owns (a) a departmental store (b) multiple shops?
questions.answer: (a) A company or business house. (b) Big manufacturers.

questions.q: State any two merits of supermarkets.
questions.answer: A wide range of daily-use goods under one roof and lower prices due to bulk purchase and avoiding middlemen.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What is a departmental store? Give any three features.
questions.answer: A large retail store selling a wide variety of goods in one building divided into departments under central management; each department sells specific goods; it provides facilities like home delivery and credit.

questions.q: What are consumer cooperative stores? State their merits.
questions.answer: Retail stores owned by cooperative societies of consumers. Merits: low prices (no middlemen), cash sales so no bad debts and profit distributed to members as bonus.

questions.q: What is a franchise form of retail trade? State any three features.
questions.answer: A franchisor allows the franchisee to use its brand and system. Features: the franchisee uses the brand name, pays a fee or royalty and follows the franchisor's standards.

questions.q: Explain any three services provided by retailers to consumers.
questions.answer: Regular supply, convenient location and wide choice (also home delivery and consumer education).

questions.q: State any three limitations of multiple shops.
questions.answer: Limited variety, only cash sales and no bargaining.

questions.q: Explain any three merits of departmental stores.
questions.answer: Goods under one roof, economies of large purchase and efficient staff.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Define a wholesaler and identify any four functions performed by them.
questions.answer: A wholesaler buys goods in bulk from manufacturers and sells to retailers. Functions: procurement of goods, grading and packing, transporting, warehousing, financing, risk bearing, market information and selling.

questions.q: Distinguish between wholesale trade and retail trade.
questions.answer: Items, quantity, source, customers, capital, relationship and display differ: wholesale deals in a few items in bulk with large capital; retail deals in a variety in small quantities near consumers.

questions.q: Explain the types of large-scale retail trade.
questions.answer: Departmental stores, multiple shops, supermarkets, consumer cooperative stores, mail order and franchise, each with features and merits.

questions.q: Explain the merits and limitations of supermarkets.
questions.answer: Merits: wide range, standard quality, cheaper goods and low operating cost; limitations: large capital, cash only and self-service limits suitable goods.

questions.q: Explain the role of middlemen in the chain of distribution.
questions.answer: Wholesalers save the producer's effort, provide credit and information; retailers supply goods to consumers, offer services and feedback; but they add to price.
